mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL annualized growth exceeds 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past two months signals weakening labor market conditions, which negatively impacts consumer spending and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases by more than 0.5pp and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over the past 3 months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST declines by more than 10% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past 3 months signals an easing monetary policy, which is generally positive for equity markets, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases over 3 months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the past month signals a strengthening labor market, which is generally positive for consumer spending and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than industrial production (INDPRO) over the past 3 months, it signals a demand-driven economy, which is positive for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > INDPRO growth in 3 months
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth exceeds INDPRO growth and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the past 3 months signals a strong supply-side response, which is generally positive for equity markets, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases by more than 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, it signals a tight labor market with high interest rates, which is negative for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: tight monetary policy with low unemployment
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is above 4% and UNRATE is below 5%, and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.
